messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: GPU pool saturation detected in us-west-2 for model v36.2. Queues increasing +1200 reqs in last 3m, avg latency 2.8s -> 6.4s, pod_p95 CPU/GPU ~98%. kv-cache prefetch amplification observed. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.example.com/d/metrics/cluster?panel=kv_prefetch

jordan (oncall): +1 oncall here. Looking. Do we have a deploy in last 30m?

sophie (eng): yes, v36.2 rollout finished 12m ago. It changed kv prefetch to aggressive prewarm (prefetch window=2048 -> 8192) to improve cold starts.

miguel (runtime): also noticed throughput per-session jump for that model. Prefetch spawns extra GPU allocations: prefetches hold KV handles that keep contexts hot. Autoscaler shows many new pods but stopped at max_pool_size=40 (we hit limit).

ashley (sre): confirmed autoscaler hit configured cap. Logs: ```autoscaler:pool_size=40 max_reached=true scale_reason=kv_prefetch_wave```

jordan (oncall): impact? Customer-facing errors?

ashley (sre): some requests are being queued and throttled — 503s count up ~180 in 10m only for customers pinned to v36.2. Non-pinned fall back to older model and are fine.

miguel (runtime): quick mitigation suggestions: 1) pause rollout (cancel canary) 2) reduce prefetch window to previous value 3) fallback to v35.x (smaller context) for heavy routes 4) temporarily increase autoscaler cap (if infra allows).

sophie (eng): I'll open a rollback/pause in rollout controller now. Command: ```./deployctl abort-rollout --model v36.2 --env prod --reason "kv-prefetch surge"```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout abort requested by sophie. ID: r-70321. Waiting for confirmation from release-controller.

jordan (oncall): while aborting, can we set `max_prefetch_sessions=4` globally for that model? Where is that config?

miguel (runtime): config path: `redwood/runtime/models/v36.2/prefetch_config`. Pushing quick patch: ```curl -X PATCH -d '{"prefetch_window":2048,"max_prefetch_sessions":4}' https://internal-api/models/v36.2/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'```

ashley (sre): I'm going to toggle a temporary route-level rate limit for heavy customers to stop amplification: ```ratectl set /api/generate customer_tier=enterprise rate=10rps```

sophie (eng): rollout controller reports abort in progress, canary pods are being drained.

miguel (runtime): autoscaler tried to request +8 GPUs from provider but hit quota. Cloud request ticket opened: CLOUD-5492 (asking to increase GPU quota in us-west-2). ETA unknown.

jordan (oncall): any immediate customer-facing comms? Should we put a short note in status.redwood.ai?

ashley (sre): customer impact limited to tenants pinned to v36.2. We'll prepare a short blurb: "We are investigating elevated latency and throttling for some customers on model v36.2 following a recent rollout. Temporary mitigations in progress."

miguel (runtime): after prefetch patch applied, we see drop in new prefetch handles. Traces: `kv.prefetch.create` down 73% in 90s. GPUs still pinned until sessions drain.

sophie (eng): can we trigger model-fallback routing to v35 for pinned tenants? I can add a quick override to routing rules. ```routingctl set-override --model v36.2 --fallback v35 --tenants tenant_list.json```

jordan (oncall): go for it, target high-rate tenants first.

ops-bot: routing-service: override applied for 6 tenants (high qps).

ashley (sre): 15m in — queue depth halved, 503s dropping. Some customers still see degraded p95.

miguel (runtime): autoscaler logs show we remain at pool_size=40, scale_requests rejected due to `max_pool_size` policy. We need emergency override to bump to 50 if infra approves.

sophie (eng): I've pinged infra slack and filed EMERGENCY-INC request. @infra-team please ack.

infra-team (external): acked — evaluating capacity options, can carve 4 GPUs from spare pools if we give us-west-2 cluster admin rights for 20m.

jordan (oncall): not ideal, but ok if it's quick. Ashley, coordinate.

ashley (sre): carving 4 GPUs now. Update autoscaler max to 50 temporarily. Command: ```kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_pool_size":"50"}}'```

ops-bot: kubectl: configmap/autoscaler-config patched

miguel (runtime): new nodes provisioning... nodesReady. Pool back to 46/50. Request queue relieved further. Latency trending down to 2.1s p95.

jordan (oncall): customer impact summary for ops: 1) 6 pinned tenants short-term throttling/503s 2) >200 requests queued briefly 3) no data loss, only latency/errors for pinned routes.

sophie (eng): we'll ship a follow-up PR to make prefetch window smaller by default and add a safety cap on prefetch sessions to prevent pool-starve. PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8421

miguel (runtime): post-mitigation steps I suggest: - revert aggressive prefetch in v36.2 - add canary checks for kv handle count before rollout bump - autoscaler should reject scale triggers from prefetch unless cpu/gpu util > threshold - add alert for `kv.prefetch.create_rate` spikes

ashley (sre): agreed. I'll open incident report and link this thread. Also sending update to affected customers. Draft message: "We've deployed temporary mitigations (fallback to v35, throttle, extra capacity) and continue to monitor. A root-cause investigation is in progress."

jordan (oncall): status page updated. Monitoring 30m. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident transitioned to MONITORING. Incident ID: INC-2026-334. Timeline: started=1719004322 mitigations_applied=1719004580 monitoring=1719004880.

sophie (eng): quick note for postmortem: include customer pinning as risk, and add opt-out guardrails for rollout changes that increase kv prefetch window.

miguel (runtime): confirmed all heavy tenants now on fallback or drained. Closing from runtime side.

jordan (oncall): closing this thread. Will follow up with postmortem draft in #postmortems. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
